cards.info: What five values make up the five-number summary?
cards.backInfo: The five-number summary consists of the Minimum, First Quartile (Q1), Median, Third Quartile (Q3), and Maximum.

cards.info: How do you find the total number of observations ($n$) from a frequency table?
cards.backInfo: Sum all the values listed in the frequency column of the table.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the steps: Sum Frequencies, Create Cumulative Counts, Find Median, Split Data, Find Q1 and Q3.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/b2d571a1-8edb-4ee8-8fe5-245646c7b02a-1786506133590-234.webp)

cards.info: What is the purpose of calculating cumulative counts in a frequency table?
cards.backInfo: Cumulative counts determine the rank-order positions (indices) occupied by each data value.

cards.info: How is the Minimum identified in a frequency distribution table?
cards.backInfo: The Minimum is the smallest data value that has a frequency greater than zero.

cards.info: How is the median calculated if the total number of observations ($n$) is even?
cards.backInfo: The median is the arithmetic average of the values at positions $n/2$ and $(n/2) + 1$.

cards.info: Where is the median located if the total number of observations ($n$) is odd?
cards.backInfo: The median is the single value located at position $(n + 1) / 2$.

cards.info: When $n$ is odd, how is the data split to find quartiles?
cards.backInfo: Exclude the median value, then split the remaining values into lower and upper halves.

cards.info: What inequality must a valid five-number summary satisfy?
cards.backInfo: It must satisfy the condition: $\text{Minimum} \le Q1 \le \text{Median} \le Q3 \le \text{Maximum}$.

cards.info: In a boxplot, what do the edges of the box represent?
cards.backInfo: The left edge of the box represents Q1 and the right edge represents Q3.

cards.info: What is a common mistake when finding the median from a frequency table?
cards.backInfo: Confusing the middle frequency number with the data value associated with the middle position.

cards.info: Which values in the five-number summary mark the ends of the boxplot whiskers?
cards.backInfo: The Minimum marks the left whisker end and the Maximum marks the right whisker end.

cards.info: If a table shows frequencies 2, 5, 4, 3, 1, what is $n$?
cards.backInfo: $n = 15$. You find this by summing all frequencies: $2 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 1$.

cards.info: If the first value has frequency 3, what positions does the next value occupy?
cards.backInfo: The next value begins at position 4 and continues for the length of its frequency.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the steps: Sum Frequencies, Create Cumulative Counts, Find Median, Split Data, Find Q1 and Q3.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/b2d571a1-8edb-4ee8-8fe5-245646c7b02a-1786506133590-234.webp)

cards.info: Can a data value with a frequency of 0 be the Minimum?
cards.backInfo: No. The Minimum must be the smallest value with a non-zero frequency.

cards.info: How is the Maximum identified in a frequency distribution table?
cards.backInfo: The Maximum is the largest data value that has a frequency greater than zero.

cards.info: If $n=20$, which two positions are averaged to find the Median?
cards.backInfo: The values at positions 10 ($n/2$) and 11 ($n/2 + 1$) are averaged.

cards.info: If $n=15$, what is the specific rank-order position of the Median?
cards.backInfo: The Median is at position 8, calculated as $(15 + 1) / 2$.

cards.info: When $n$ is even, how many elements are in each half for quartiles?
cards.backInfo: The dataset is split into two equal halves, each containing $n/2$ elements.

cards.info: Why is the median excluded when calculating quartiles for an odd $n$?
cards.backInfo: Excluding the median ensures the remaining data is split into two equal-sized halves.

cards.info: What is the formal definition of the First Quartile (Q1)?
cards.backInfo: Q1 is the median of the lower half of the sorted dataset.
